messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need per-model/route SLO dashboards for latency + throughput before the next release. P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec. Can runtime/infra provide stable metrics (with useful labels) by next Wed?

ajay: We can. Runtime currently exposes inference latency histograms and token counters, but labels are only {pool, host}. We'll need to add {model, route, deployment, rollout_version}.

kyle: Cardinality warning — model x route combos can explode. Do we have an expected cardinality estimate? If high, we should plan bucketing/rollup or sampling.

sophie: Console product wants small per-route tiles: single-number P50/P95/P99 + 1m sparkline and a regression flag if P95 >20% baseline. Also want a canary vs prod compare view.

ajay: Proposal from runtime side: export metrics with these canonical names/labels: inference_latency_ms (histogram) with labels {model_id, route_id, deployment, rollout}, inference_ttft_ms (summary), inference_tokens_per_sec (gauge) with same labels. For very high-card models we can emit route_hash instead of full route_id and add sample_rate label.

kyle: Sounds fine if we constrain label cardinality. Prefer normalized model_id (no freeform semver strings) and a model_variant enum. We'll enforce max label cardinality in metrics pipeline.

sophie: Also need aggregation windows: tokens/sec aggregated 1m and 5m; latency percentiles at 1m and 5m. TTFT should be corrected for streaming (time-to-first-token when first token sent, not entire response).

ajay: Yep — runtime will compute TTFT on the server side and expose inference_ttft_ms. For streaming, we emit two counters: ttft_event{streaming="true"} and ttft_event{streaming="false"}. Example prometheus-style lines to illustrate: 

```
# EXAMPLE
inference_latency_ms_bucket{model_id="gpt-4o-mini",route_id="chat_start",le="50"} 123
inference_latency_ms_bucket{model_id="gpt-4o-mini",route_id="chat_start",le="100"} 456
inference_ttft_ms{model_id="gpt-4o-mini",route_id="chat_start"} 45
inference_tokens_per_sec{model_id="gpt-4o-mini",route_id="chat_start"} 320.5
```

ajay: We'll also propagate a header x-redwood-rollout so console and telemetry can map requests to canary/prod variants.

kyle: We'll add a metric scrubber step in the pipeline to roll up rare labels into "other" buckets and limit series churn. Also suggest a route sampling plan: full resolution for top N routes, hashed sampling for the rest.

sophie: For the dashboard UX: add a 'compare to baseline' control (7d/30d), show tokens/sec, request rate, and a tiny table of models driving the most latency. Also a toggle to view canary vs prod side-by-side.

maria: Action items: runtime -> emit proposed labels + header propagation (ajay), infra -> implement cardinality scrubbing + aggregation windows (kyle), console -> prototype tiles and regression rules (sophie). Can everyone confirm ETA?

ajay: ETA: labels and header in staging by Tue EOD, basic metrics pipeline changes in staging shortly after.

sophie: I'll mock tiles and attach screenshots by Wed.

kyle: I'll add scrubbing rules and a short doc about cardinality limits by Wed as well.

infra-bot: deploy: runtime/telemetry v2 rolled to staging at 1764000200 :rocket:

maria: Great. @sre FYI — we may need extra scrape capacity when this goes prod.

kyle: :thumbsup: I'll coordinate with SRE once staging looks stable.

maria: I'll open the dashboard PR on Thursday and link RFC notes. Thanks all.

ajay: One more note — include rollout_version label so we can do canary regressions in dashboards (P95 delta). We'll also emit request_id and trace_id for a subset of requests to wire up traces for regressions.

sophie: Perfect, that's all we need to implement the regression alerting UX.

maria: Closing loop — I'll post a short summary + checklist to the eng-platform doc tonight.
